clue.text: Two men of the match these days maybe

definitions.text: Two men of the match these days maybe

parts.words: Two men of the match these days maybe
parts.note: a match is also a wedding, and nowadays both partners in one may be men, playing on the sporting award man of the match

explanation.surface: A football report wondering whether two players might share the man-of-the-match award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a sporting fixture, but here it is a marriage; 'these days maybe' nods to same-sex marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedded pair is the result of a match in the matrimonial sense, so two men so joined form one.

clue.text: True, prior's home is wrong for a leading nun

indicators.note: is wrong says the letters are set out in an incorrect order

parts.note: the s of the possessive counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: Truly, a monastery head's house is unsuitable for a senior nun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prior' looks like the monastic title that fits the nun, but it is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a convent of nuns holds this title, so she leads the community.

clue.text: Willing to study and study ultimately

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the second study

explanation.surface: A keen student happy to study and keep on studying.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prepared and eager to do something is a synonym of being willing.

clue.text: Silly banalities that could describe monstrous appetite

indicators.note: silly means foolish or messed up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Foolish clichés used to talk about a giant hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite that can never be satisfied is a monstrous one, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Party with old man engaging women in entrance

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: Ray is a man's name

explanation.surface: A partygoer and an elderly man chatting up women at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old man' looks like one piece but splits into O and RAY; 'engaging' puts W inside RAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening through which one enters a building is its entrance.

clue.text: Great anger brought by ending of power in electricity failure

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the other piece

parts.note: an outage is a cut in the power supply

indicators.note: ending of picks the final letter of power

explanation.surface: A power cut leaves people furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury or indignation at something shocking is great anger.

clue.text: Dad achieved victory after losing middle piece on board

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: losing middle means the central letter is dropped

parts.note: won means achieved a victory

explanation.surface: Dad wins a game after sacrificing a central chessman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing middle' takes O out of WON, leaving WN.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowliest chessman is one of the pieces on a chessboard.

clue.text: Fanatic no longer, mister having reformed over time

indicators.note: over says the earlier pieces sit above the last one in this down entry

parts.note: ex means former, no longer

indicators.note: having reformed means made again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former zealot, now a gentleman who has mended his ways over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having reformed' turns MISTER into TREMIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot holding radical views is a synonym of fanatic.

clue.text: Let pen fly with memos here and there, working with no concern for boss?

definitions.text: working with no concern for boss?

indicators.note: here and there means scattered about, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: An office worker scattering memos without caring what the boss thinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Working for yourself means having no employer, so no boss to worry about.

clue.text: Puff-puff I missed going to game — get bus maybe?

indicators.note: missed says the letter given by the word I goes absent from the train

parts.note: puff-puff is a child's word for a steam train
a sport is a game

explanation.surface: A child's steam train is off the menu, so it's the bus to the match instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed' drops I from TRAIN, leaving TRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is one example of public conveyance, so the question mark signals definition by example.

clue.text: Bit of willow to dry up almost entirely

indicators.note: almost entirely says the word is taken all but its final letter

parts.note: to wither is to dry up and shrivel

explanation.surface: Advice to let a cut willow twig dry out nearly completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' cuts the last letter, R, off WITHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A withe is a flexible willow twig used for tying or basket-making.

clue.text: Country type agitated about end of hunting

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
agitated means stirred up, so the letters of type are shaken into a new order
end of picks the final letter of hunting

explanation.surface: Some kind of nation gets upset when its hunting season closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' turns TYPE into EYPT; 'about' wraps that round G, the end of 'hunting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a nation of North Africa, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Waste away in northern river

definitions.meaning: to erode or be worn down by use
the river flowing through Durham and Sunderland in north-east England

explanation.surface: Something wasting away in a river up north.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in north-east England, running through Durham to Sunderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one spelling: erosion by use, and the name of a river in County Durham.

clue.text: Receiving no sound ideas, is put off female

indicators.note: put off means removed, so the two letters of the word is are taken out of ideas

explanation.surface: Someone's ideas are rejected by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is put off' removes I and S from IDEAS, leaving DEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to hear perceives nothing audible, so they receive no sound.

clue.text: A snack for your setter?

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog as well as the compiler of a crossword

explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' suggests the crossword's compiler, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A biscuit given as a treat to a canine is a snack for a pet such as a setter.

clue.text: Brief? That sounds like our warm season

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is spoken the same as the following word

parts.note: summery means belonging to the warm season of the year

explanation.surface: A lawyer's brief described as sunny and seasonal.
explanation.walkthrough: SUMMERY, like summer, and SUMMARY, a brief account, are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is a short account of the essentials, a synonym for a précis.

clue.text: Muddle with man in charge aiming to rescue the situation?

parts.note: a mess is a muddle
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A confused man in authority trying to sort things out.
explanation.definitionFit: A messiah is a saviour, so someone with saviour-like zeal aims to rescue things.

clue.text: Part one got is making for self-regard

indicators.note: Part says a portion of the following words, running across them, gives the answer

explanation.surface: A sentence about one person's role being self-centred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' signals letters spanning 'onE GOT IS Making'.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive self-regard and conceit are synonyms for vanity of this kind.

clue.text: Nasty little creature was first to be found in ground

parts.note: a pest is an annoying small animal or insect
to have led is to have been first or in front

explanation.surface: A horrid little creature led the way into the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil but is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Crushed with a pestle in a mortar means pounded or milled fine.

clue.text: Like some divers stuck initially in river plant

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: a pea is a plant

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of stuck

explanation.surface: Divers getting stuck in weed at the start of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers who work far below the surface of the ocean are described with this adjective.

clue.text: Like a sort of road test with piece inserted

indicators.note: inserted says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A road test with a piece of extra track added.
explanation.walkthrough: An orbital road is a ring road circling a city, like London's M25.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring road around a city is described as encircling, hence the adjective for it.

clue.text: Lack of transparency in a business community undermining work

indicators.note: undermining says the following pieces go beneath the first in this down entry

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Murky dealings in a business community that is sabotaging a job.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the City of London, Britain's financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opaque, not letting light through, is the noun for a lack of clarity.

clue.text: Very bright person avoids having head in shower

indicators.note: avoids having head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a brain is a very clever person

explanation.surface: A clever person dodges a wet head in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' is weather, not a bathroom fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief fall of precipitation from clouds is a shower.

clue.text: Some behaved abominably in holy book

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaving in a sacred scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vedas are the ancient Hindu scriptures written in Sanskrit.

clue.text: Secret agent admits nothing having earlier captured English soldier

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so another piece goes inside
having earlier captured says the agent already holds one letter inside

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A spy who once seized an English soldier lets nothing slip.
explanation.walkthrough: SPY first takes in E (SEPY), then admits O.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepoy was an Indian infantryman serving under British command.

clue.text: Identify fish, one getting away

indicators.note: getting away says the letter escapes from the fish

parts.note: plaice is a flatfish
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Spotting a fish as one escapes the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Identify' as in 'I can't place him', to recognise.
explanation.definitionFit: To recognise or pin down who someone is, as in failing to put a name to a face.

clue.text: Loud organ to convey terror

parts.note: F is forte, the musical instruction for loud
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A noisy church organ used to frighten people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the instrument beside 'Loud', but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread and fright are synonyms for strong alarm.

clue.text: Oz no longer welcoming for people of taste?

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in another piece

parts.note: once means formerly, no longer so
U means upper-class, acceptable to refined people

explanation.surface: Australia is no longer hospitable to discerning folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oz' looks like Australia but is the abbreviation for a weight; U is the old label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Oz is the standard abbreviation of the imperial unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: Encourage one getting cross no end to go into country

indicators.note: to go into says the pieces are put inside the other

parts.note: a state is a country
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: no end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

explanation.surface: Urging someone, irritable without end, to move abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' trims MULE to MUL; 'cross' looks like angry but is a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur on or rouse someone to action is a synonym of urging them.

clue.text: Any barters etc to be arranged in London thoroughfare

indicators.note: to be arranged says the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Trading deals and so on to be set up on a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: Carnaby Street is a fashion shopping street in London's Soho, famous in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a named street in the West End of the capital, so a city thoroughfare.
